newsitem.title: ITALY: Elsag Bailey sees Q4 orders at $440-450 mln.
newsitem.headline: Elsag Bailey sees Q4 orders at $440-450 mln.

text.p: Elsag Bailey, a company controlled by Italian state group Finmeccanica, is hoping for "very good" fourth quarter 1996 orders after a period of weakness, and sees a strong rebound in the quarter's results.

"The last part of the year is traditionally the best for us, October went well, November and December could also be better. We have orders of between $440-450 million," the group's chief executive, Vincenzo Cannatelli, said at the presentation of one the group's new products.
Cannatelli declined to forecast net results, but he did say that net operating profit "is seen 40/50 percent better at around $55 million".

Elsag Bailey has spend most of the year seeking to reduce overall costs and to restructure. The group said in October that it saw fourth quarter earnings below analysts' expectations but the company added that it expected its financial performance for the quarter to rebound.
The company supplies process automation systems, instrumentation products, analytical measurement devices and related professional services.
The shares of Elsag Bailey, quoted on Wall Street, have been recently depressed due to provisions for the fourth quarter which followed weakness in orders in the second and third quarters.

Looking ahead, Cannatelli said that 1997 would be positive in term of sales and profits. He said that 1997 would be a year of consolidation and growth after the last of the group's restructuring was completed. The group has already cut 1,200 jobs from the 1,800 forecast.
